questions.prompt: Given a sorted list of integers and a target value, report whether any two different positions hold values that add up to the target.
questions.relevance_to_role: The job description asks for strong array and string problem solving.
questions.expected_answer: Use two indices, one at each end. If the sum is too small move the left index right, if too large move the right index left, until they meet.

rubric.criterion: Recognises the sorted input allows two pointers
States O(n) time and O(1) space

follow_ups: How would this change if the list were not sorted?
common_mistakes: Using nested loops (O(n^2)) without noticing the sorted order
Allowing the same position to be used twice
questions.notes: Fictional example of a single, unverified candidate report.

coding.problem_statement: Given a non-decreasing list of integers and an integer target, determine whether two different positions i and j exist with values[i] + values[j] equal to target.
coding.input_format: First line: n and target. Second line: n integers in non-decreasing order.
edge_cases: the target needs the same value at two different positions

questions.prompt: A table of employees and a table of departments are joined so that every employee appears even if their department is missing. Which join does this?
questions.relevance_to_role: The job description lists SQL basics.
questions.expected_answer: A LEFT JOIN from employees to departments.

rubric.criterion: Chooses the join that keeps all employees

follow_ups: What does the department column contain for an employee with no department?
common_mistakes: Choosing INNER JOIN, which drops employees without a department
questions.notes: Written to test a skill the job description requires; nobody is claimed to have been asked it.

options: LEFT JOIN from employees to departments
RIGHT JOIN from employees to departments
mcq.explanation: A LEFT JOIN keeps every row of the left table (employees) and fills missing department values with NULL.
mcq.distractor_notes: INNER JOIN is the common wrong answer; RIGHT JOIN from employees keeps every department instead.

questions.prompt: Describe a time you disagreed with a teammate about how to build something. How did you reach a decision?
questions.relevance_to_role: The job description lists teamwork and communication.
questions.expected_answer: A specific situation, what the candidate did to understand the other view, how the decision was made, and what was learned.

rubric.criterion: Listens and weighs the other view

follow_ups: What would you do differently now?
common_mistakes: A vague answer with no concrete example
questions.notes: Practice question for preparation; not claimed to be asked by any company.

behavioral.star_guidance: Situation: the project and the disagreement. Task: your responsibility. Action: how you listened and proposed a way forward. Result: the decision and what you learned.
positive_signals: Uses data or a small experiment to decide
